## Why it happens

DSH normalizes attachments before storing them, and `dsh-attachment-local` picks
the container from

achments before storing them, and `dsh-attachment-local` picks
the container from the alpha channel:

Screenshots have an alpha channel, so they are stored as WebP. The request-image
ladder only ever em

its `alpha:webp` or `opaque:jpeg` — there is no PNG rung and no
configuration option for this.

`dsh-llm-pi-ai` then builds the OpenAI `image_url` payload straight from the
prepared request image:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

so the wire payload becomes `data:image/webp;base64,...`. LM Studio / llama.cpp
validate that label

against a PNG/JPEG allowlist and reject the whole call —
even though the bytes decode perfectly well

even though the bytes decode perfectly well.
## How it works

Wrap `attachments.readImageRequest()` and return **the same bytes** under a
compatible label:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Measured against LM Studio with `test/diagnostics/relabel-vs-transcode.py`:
| Payload | Result |

| webp bytes + `image/webp` | **HTTP 400** `'url' field must be a base64 encoded image.` |
| webp by

tes + `image/png`  | **HTTP 200**, image correctly understood |
| png bytes + `image/png`   | HTTP 2

00 |
| png bytes + `image/webp`  | **HTTP 400** |

Only the label is validated, so no image transcoding is needed.
`test/diagnostics/vision-read.py` co

nfirms the model really sees the image:
it reads a word drawn into a WebP image sent as `image/png`.
Three implementation details matter, and each was verified rather than assumed:

- **Why not rewrite the request messages?** The adapter takes the label from
`readImageRequest(...).

mediaType`, not from the message's
`ImageBlock.attachment.mediaType`. Rewriting messages changes not

hing.
- **Why is a service patch picked up immediately?** The adapter resolves the
service per call

(`resolveAttachments: () => ctx.get("attachments")`), so
wrapping the method affects the very next r

equest — no restart, no new session.
- **Why the prototype instead of the instance?** `ctx.get()` re

turns a Cordis
"traceable" `Proxy` whose `set` trap routes through an extra shadow receiver, so
an i

nstance-level write is not reliably observable. A property on the prototype
is always found by the p
roxy's own descriptor walk.

The model-visible attachment handle text is unaffected: it is built from
`ref.mediaType`, not `versi

on.mediaType`, so it still describes the stored WebP
accurately.

## Verify it works
With `debug: true` the DSH console prints one line per relabeled image:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

You can also check the model server's own request log: the payload should contain
`"url": "data:imag
e/png;base64,..."` rather than `image/webp`.
## Disable / uninstall

Disable the plugin in the DSH plugin manager, or set `to: image/webp` in the
config. Either way the

original `readImageRequest` is restored from the saved
descriptor — the patch is fully reversible.
## Limitations

- **The label does not match the container.** The bytes stay WebP while the label
says PNG. This is

correct for servers that validate the label (LM Studio,
llama.cpp). A provider that strictly validat

es magic bytes would still reject
it, and the right fix there is real transcoding (`sharp`, `sips`)

rather than
relabeling.
- **It applies to every provider,** because `readImageRequest()` cannot see

which
route the call is going to. Scoping it to local routes would need an extra
`llm/stream` listen

er keyed by `options.provider`.
- **It depends on DSH internals:** the `attachments` service, its
`r

eadImageRequest` method, and that method being a class method on the
prototype. If a DSH upgrade bre
aks it, those are the two things to check.
